articles.title: Sali Hughes on beauty: a buzzy new brand is aimed at women over 40 – and the industry is taking notice
articles.summary: Beauty mogul Sarah Creal decided there was too much emphasis on the teen market – so she designed a range of products for older women. Now others are following suit. It’s rare that I devote a whole column to one brand, but not as rare as the decision by any beauty company to back women over 40, so…
body: Creal, co-creator of Victoria Beckham Beauty and product developer of countless global companies for more than 30 years, felt that women of her generation (she’s 56) and their specific beauty challenges (hooded eyelids, decreased product wear time and so on) were being overlooked by major brands in favour of teenagers. Wander into any lip-oil slicked, Korean sheet-mask filled, freckle-pen-dotted branch of Sephora and tell me she’s wrong.

Creal, a New Yorker who recognised the buying power of what will perhaps be the last generation of consumers to have done better than their parents, decided to build an entire brand for mature, busy women with a love of luxury and a bathroom cabinet full of products that no longer serve them. The buzz around her 2024 US launch had me walking from one Manhattan Sephora to the next, buying whatever scraps I could lay my hands on. But it’s the quality of the products that kept me refilling at each visit.
points: Beauty mogul Sarah Creal decided there was too much emphasis on the teen market – so she designed a range of products for older women.

articles.title: The secret lives of men who read romance books: ‘My life is full of love, so I’m drawn to them’
articles.summary: It’s often assumed straight men are not interested in romantic fiction – but many are sharing their passion in forums online. After a tiring day as a school maintenance worker, 28-year-old Paul loves nothing more than unwinding with a good romance novel – ideally one with a fantasy or horror…
body: Paul got into romance fiction via what he calls its “more traditional” side – such as the Regency romance series Bridgerton. He is partially sighted, so he mostly reads on his Kindle, where he can adjust the font size. In the first Bridgerton novel, “Simon, the main character, has a speech impediment that he has to work through,” says Paul. “I’m more attached to that one. Typically, I don’t come across disabled protagonists that much.”

Straight men like Paul who read and write romance are largely invisible to the wider world. Women are the genre’s main audience, followed by queer romance, which is a well documented success. The fifth volume of Alice Oseman’s Heartstopper – about the friendship between two teenage boys blossoming into love – is the UK’s fastest-selling graphic novel and a hit Netflix show, while novelists such as Alexis Hall are widely read and critically acclaimed. But in this corner of publishing, straight men are rarely seen and usually stigmatised.
points: It’s often assumed straight men are not interested in romantic fiction – but many are sharing their passion in forums online.

articles.title: ‘Delays are always welcome’: 10 of the best railway station pubs in England
articles.summary: Converted from Victorian buffet bars, ticket offices and waiting rooms, these station pubs offer beautifully restored interiors, real ales and a slice of railway history.
body: No prizes for guessing what this pub used to be… The Old Ticket Office has high ceilings, walls painted shades of locomotive green and booths resembling train carriages; there are outdoor tables on Station Square. A live train departures board theoretically prevents passengers lingering too long, and a canning machine means any draught beer is also available to take away (the hatch on platform 4 also does takeaway orders). There are five handpulls plus Young’s usual spritz menu and other drinks, plus light bites and pizzas. The pub is currently closed for roof repairs and expected to reopen by the end of October.

articles.title: A moment that changed me: My mother fell off a mountain – and my life began again
articles.summary: A bad breakup had made me afraid I would be mired in anger for ever. But on that family hike, in our fear and horror as we awaited the air ambulance, my old hurts took on a different hue. To steal a well-known line, 2023 is not a year on which I shall look back with undiluted pleasure.
body: Ordinarily, my work would have been my solace; when I wrote, it was as if time was suspended. But now, my words abandoned me. They would not come, no matter how much I tried. So, in April, I decided to take the rest of the year off to recover. As I was self-employed, this was not a choice I made lightly – but my heart was broken and so too, it seemed, was my brain.

As befitting a millennial woman who read Eat Pray Love at a formative age, I attempted to recover using every kind of therapy imaginable. Unfortunately, even after a five-week trip to Thailand for a yoga and wellness retreat, I didn’t feel “healed”. I still felt resentful and sad, and I became afraid that I would be mired in my anger for the rest of my life.

That September, my father turned 63. He didn’t want presents; he wanted the whole family – my parents, me, my sister and her now husband – to climb Carrauntoohil, the highest mountain in Ireland, together.

articles.title: Brooklyn and Nicola Peltz Beckham Bring Their Best Basics to Paris Fashion Week
articles.summary: After a recent return to the spotlight in dramatic red carpet looks, Brooklyn and Nicola Peltz Beckham begin PFW decidedly low-key.
body: Paris Fashion Week may reliably inspire celebrities to indulge their more sensual side—Zoë Kravitz gave naked dressing a fall update at Saint Laurent yesterday, while Rihanna kicked off the week at Matières Fécales in a shimmering bronze skirt suit —but Brooklyn and Nicola Peltz Beckham are taking a rather more low-key approach to dressing in the French capital.

For a date night in Paris, Nicola reached for something considerably simpler, sporting a white Cou Cou Intimates Rina top, an Instagram Explore page totem, with three-quarter-length sleeves and a curved hemline. She paired it with low-rise black leather trousers, pointed black pumps, a rectangular shoulder bag, and oversized sunglasses—the latter a practical defense against the wall of camera flashes waiting outside.

It’s a familiar proposition for Nicola Peltz Beckham. Away from the red carpet, the actor regularly gravitates towards an elevated take on basics: little white tops, tanks, straight-leg denim, leather trousers, and slinky ’90s-inflected separates are recurring fixtures in her wardrobe. And in terms of glam, her chest-length brunette hair was worn in soft, blown-out waves.
points: After a recent return to the spotlight in dramatic red carpet looks, Brooklyn and Nicola Peltz Beckham begin PFW decidedly low-key.

articles.title: The Inside Story of Balmain’s Transformation
articles.summary: CEO Matteo Sgarbossa and CMO Bruna Scognamiglio have spent the last two years redefining Balmain across product, retail, and pricing, along with new creative director Antonin Tron. Ahead of tonight’s show, they reveal exactly how they did it.
body: When the shutters opened just before the models walked Antonin Tron’s debut show for Balmain last season, the symbolism was hard to escape. Tron took the creative director chair to let the light of a new day in for the Parisian house.

But as it goes, Tron’s appointment was only one part of the story. Behind the scenes, CEO Matteo Sgarbossa had been leading a thorough transformation of the Mayhoola-owned company since he took on the role in May 2024. Two months later, he found a new CMO in Bruna Scognamiglio and appointed Tron in November 2025, a little after the departure of Olivier Rousteing, who had been at the helm for 14 years.

Together, they have been rethinking Balmain’s product, stores, pricing and communication strategies. Ahead of tonight’s show, we sat down with Matteo and Bruna to get the inside story of Balmain’s transformation strategy.
Vogue: You both recently celebrated your two-year anniversary at Balmain. What would you say have been your biggest moments so far?

articles.title: 47 Easy Make-Ahead Thanksgiving Sides
articles.summary: Despite your most careful planning (did you make a detailed timeline?), cooking Thanksgiving dinner can still feel a little stressful once the big day rolls around. It holds true whether you’re having a small Thanksgiving dinner or hosting the whole extended family.
body: From classic stuffing to cozy and creamy casseroles, we’ve rounded up 47 make-ahead Thanksgiving sides that can be prepped, assembled, or even totally cooked anywhere from a day to a month in advance.

Stuffing is a great make-ahead side. Depending on your schedule and energy level, you’ve got a couple of options. For a head start, simply toast the bread up to several days in advance. Or if you prefer to tackle a little more, the whole dish can be prepped and assembled, then stashed in the fridge until you’re ready to slide it into the oven.

Roasted turkey gets the magazine covers and the big platters, but stuffing is the real star of the show. We're talking classic, herby, moist, and fragrant bread stuffing — just like your favorite boxed stuffing mix, but even better.

This hearty stuffing has all the flavors of French onion soup. It’s packed with deeply caramelized onions cooked low and slow until sweet and jammy, then topped with Gruyère cheese and broiled until melted and gooey.

articles.title: How Claudio Antonioli Rebuilt Ann Demeulemeester’s Cult Following
articles.summary: After building and selling New Guards Group to Farfetch, the entrepreneur bought indie label Ann Demeulemeester, which he has spent six years restoring back to its original glory. Ahead of tonight’s Paris store opening and Saturday show, he sits down with Vogue.
body: If anyone needed proof that subcultures still exist, all they needed to do was walk into the Parisian friary that housed last season’s Ann Demeulemeester runway show on the Saturday evening of Paris Fashion Week.

A musical duo called Beguiling Junior played husky rock music as about 500 20-year-olds all decked in Ann Demeulemeester took their seats around the vaulted space. Led Zeppelin guitarist Jimmy Page sat across from me, while one row behind him and to the right, a couple was making out throughout the show, his messy hair buried in her neck, her pale pink chiffon dress draped across his leather jacket. If that couple looked up, they’d have seen Billy Idol walk.
“This is such a scene,” breathed British Vogue ’s Julia Hobbs, sitting next to me.

articles.title: Esmé Creed-Miles Takes Us Behind the Scenes of ‘Sense and Sensibility’
articles.summary: A new film adaptation of Jane Austen’s “Sense and Sensibility” reimagines a tale of the unshakeable bonds of sisterhood. On set, actor Esmé Creed-Miles turned the camera on her co-stars, including Daisy Edgar-Jones, capturing moments of boundless creativity and friendship.
body: This story originally appeared in the October 2026 issue of Vogue Australia.

Of all the images Esmé Creed-Miles took on the set of Sense and Sensibility, there is one she loves the most. It depicts star Daisy Edgar-Jones, raven hair swept from her face, looking at Creed-Miles behind her camera. Edgar-Jones is held by actor George MacKay, who gazes at her with such tenderness.
“This should be the poster,” Creed-Miles says definitively. “It could be on the side of a bus.”

The novel—previously adapted by Emma Thompson into a beloved film—ripples with wit, and with the insights of a woman who was herself devoted to her sister. For Austen, the hurdles placed between a pair of lovers are commensurate with the distress of seeing a sister broken-hearted. “All of this has been going on at a time when, as you too well know, it has not been my only unhappiness,” Elinor tells Marianne. “If you can think me capable of ever feeling, surely you may suppose I have suffered now.”

articles.title: 23 Thanksgiving Turkey Recipes for Every Kind of Gathering
articles.summary: Whole birds, turkey breasts, braised legs, and more ways to rule the Thanksgiving table.
body: Picking a Thanksgiving turkey recipe is not very different from dating. Hear us out: There are plenty of great options, but you have to find the one that fits your life. How big is your gathering? How big is your oven? Should you even use the oven? Or is the grill calling your name? Maybe you're ready to venture away from your usual type. Or maybe you’re looking for something dependable, just this once.

If you want us to make the decision for you, start with our go-to Thanksgiving turkey: a whole bird dry-brined for juicy meat, slathered with butter, and finished with a tangy honey glaze for crispy, deeply browned skin. It’s the turkey we return to year after year.

But there's more than one way to put turkey on the Thanksgiving table. Spatchcocking means faster, more even cooking and plenty of crispy skin; turkey breast makes sense for a smaller gathering; braised legs put dark meat front and center; and a grilled or smoked turkey frees up precious oven space. Below, you’ll find 23 Thanksgiving turkey recipes for whatever kind of holiday you're hosting.
There’s the fast way, the better way—and one method that doesn’t require thawing at all.
